author: Robert Carr
description: Lightly seared chicken and broccoli in an orange, ginger, garlic, and toasted-sesame sauce, served with brown rice.
equipment: 12-inch nonstick or well-seasoned skillet with a lid
Saucepan with a tight-fitting lid, or rice cooker
Small bowl and whisk for sauce
Measuring cups and spoons; fine grater
Knife and separate cutting boards for produce and raw chicken
Shallow refrigerator- and freezer-safe containers, for meal prep

groceryIngredients.note: Plain, unbrined chicken without added salt solution; about 680 g.
Plain dry rice; a standard US measuring cup, about 180 g.
About 454 g; 1 1/2-inch florets with thick stems sliced thinly.
Medium sweet oranges, for 1/2 cup juice and 2 tsp finely grated zest. Measure the yield.
Reduced-sodium, about 590 mg sodium per tablespoon; check the label, not regular soy sauce.
Unseasoned; not sweetened seasoned rice vinegar.
For two batches of chicken and the aromatics.
For finishing; not the chicken searing oil.
Thinly sliced; keep white/light-green parts separate from dark-green tops.

ingredients: 1 1/2 lb (680 g) boneless skinless chicken breast, plain and unbrined, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 cup dry brown basmati rice, about 180 g; use a standard US measuring cup
1 3/4 cups water for rice, or the amount on its package, plus 1/4 cup for broccoli and 1/4 cup for sauce
1 lb (454 g) broccoli florets, about 1 1/2 inches wide, with thick stems sliced thinly
2 medium sweet oranges, for 1/2 cup fresh juice and 2 teaspoons finely grated zest
4 teaspoons cornstarch, divided: 2 teaspoons chicken and 2 teaspoons sauce
1 1/2 tablespoons canola oil, divided: 2 teaspoons per chicken batch and 1/2 teaspoon aromatics
3 green onions, thinly sliced, whites and greens separated
instructions: Start the rice first and prepare the other ingredients while it cooks. Rinse and drain the rice, combine with 1 3/4 cups water in a saucepan, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low for about 40 minutes. Remove from heat and rest covered for 10 minutes. Follow the package ratio and timing when different; no oil or salt is needed. If still firm and dry, add 1 to 2 tablespoons water and cook covered a little longer.

Wash and prepare produce before handling raw chicken. Grate 2 teaspoons orange zest without the white pith, then squeeze and measure 1/2 cup juice. Whisk the juice, soy sauce, vinegar, honey, 1/4 cup water, 2 teaspoons cornstarch, and optional red pepper in a clean bowl. Keep the zest, sesame oil, ginger, garlic, and sliced green onions separate. Pat chicken dry, cut evenly, and toss with the remaining 2 teaspoons cornstarch. Do not rinse chicken; wash hands and clean its preparation surfaces afterward.

When the rice has about 20 minutes left including its rest, put the broccoli and 1/4 cup water in the skillet over medium-high heat. Cover and steam for 3 to 4 minutes until bright green and just tender-crisp. Transfer to a bowl and carefully drain any remaining water; dry the skillet. The broccoli will finish in the sauce.

Heat 2 teaspoons canola oil in the skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering, not smoking. Spread half the chicken in one layer. Leave undisturbed for about 2 minutes, then turn and cook 3 to 5 minutes more, until lightly golden and the thickest pieces reach 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Transfer to a clean plate. Repeat with another 2 teaspoons oil and the remaining chicken. Reduce heat if the coating darkens too fast; do not crowd the pan or keep cooking done chicken for a darker crust.

Reduce heat to medium and add the remaining 1/2 teaspoon canola oil, ginger, garlic, and green-onion whites. Stir for 30 seconds until fragrant, without browning the garlic. Whisk the sauce again to lift settled starch, pour it in, and simmer while stirring for 1 to 2 minutes until glossy and lightly thickened. Return the broccoli and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until tender to your liking; then add the already-cooked chicken and its juices just long enough to coat and warm through. Add a tablespoon of water if the sauce becomes sticky or too thick rather than reducing it into a syrup.

Remove from heat and stir in the orange zest, toasted sesame oil, and green-onion tops. Divide the rice and chicken-broccoli mixture equally among four plates or shallow containers. Serve immediately, or begin rapid cooling for meal prep as described in the notes.
notes: Allow about 60 to 65 minutes with regular brown rice and about 25 minutes of hands-on work. Plain quick-cooking brown rice can shorten dinner to about 30 to 35 minutes: use enough dry rice to yield roughly 3 cups cooked, following its package. For a rice cooker, use the correct brown-rice setting and matching cup/water instructions; start early enough for its full cycle.

Sweet orange juice supplies most of the sweetness; zest and toasted sesame oil go in off heat for a fresher finish. Measure the honey rather than using a sweet bottled orange sauce. Use unseasoned vinegar and reduced-sodium soy sauce; no extra salt, stock, hoisin, or soy drizzle is included. Reduced-sodium soy sauce still contains substantial sodium. This recipe contains soy and sesame, and usually wheat from soy sauce.

The light cornstarch coating helps the sauce cling; this is not a breaded or crispy fried dish. Stir the sauce just before adding because cornstarch settles. Batch-sear the chicken and briefly finish it in the sauce to avoid drying it out. For eight servings, cook the skillet portion in separate batches.

Meal prep with rice: Use the conservative UK Food Standards Agency plan of refrigerating only portions to be eaten within 24 hours and freezing the rest. Divide rice promptly after its rest into shallow portions and cool rapidly, ideally within 1 hour of cooking; a cold-water bath around a shallow metal container can help. Do not leave rice in the pot to cool. Refrigerate or freeze promptly, with the refrigerator at 40 degrees F or below and freezer at 0 degrees F or below. Refrigerate other cooked food within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90 degrees F.

Pack rice beside the sauced chicken and broccoli, label the date, and aim to use frozen meals within 2 months for quality. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator and use within 24 hours of thawing. Reheat rice only once and eat promptly; reheating does not make poorly stored rice safe. For meal prep, cook a fresh batch of rice rather than reheating frozen rice, chilling it again, and reheating it later.

Reheating: Thaw one frozen portion overnight in the refrigerator. Add 1 to 2 tablespoons water, cover with a microwave-safe vented lid, and heat at medium to medium-high power in 60-second intervals, stirring or turning between intervals. Use shorter intervals near the end. After a 1-minute stand, check several spots with a thermometer and continue until all hot components reach 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Reheat only the portion being eaten and serve promptly. Add the water mainly to the rice; the sauce will loosen when stirred. Frozen broccoli will be softer, not crisp, after reheating.

Frozen broccoli works by equal weight. Cook according to its package, drain well, and add when the sauce is thickened instead of using the fresh-broccoli steaming step. Excess thawed water dilutes the sauce. Avoid seasoned bags and keep the measured oil and soy sauce unchanged.
title: Orange-Ginger Chicken with Broccoli and Brown Rice
